items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You remember someone named Damita Jo?

ctx.x: Della Reese came to Washington. She was down on the corner at a fine joint, and I was at the Brass Rail, but I had a good audience. And I had to go to see her, because John Levy was in town. He said, ―I want you to, when you get done, we‘ll go down and meet Della.‖ Well, when we walked in the door, Della was, boy, she was laying somebody out. Boy, she could do it, and she was built, I mean, really built. Everything was so tight, it was like she could hardly breathe, and these things were bulging out, and then she…
Oh yes, she was beautiful. She was beautiful.
